q.t: The Moon shines by…
q.e: It emits no light of its own.

q.t: The full Moon is called…
q.e: Amavasya is the new Moon.

q.t: The new Moon is called…
q.e: Only the dark half faces us.

q.t: One full Moon to the next takes about…
q.e: The basis of the month.

q.t: The Earth's revolution around the Sun takes about…
q.e: The basis of the year.

q.t: The mean solar day is…
q.e: Highest Sun to highest Sun, averaged.

q.t: The calendar used worldwide today is the…
q.e: Months total 365 days.

q.t: The Moon rises about how many minutes later each day?
q.e: Because it has moved along its orbit.

q.t: Who is the Father of the Indian Space Programme?
q.e: He pioneered India's first satellite effort.

q.t: The Moon is Earth's…
q.e: Human-made satellites are artificial.

q.t: What causes the Moon's phases?
o: Changing positions of Sun, Moon and Earth
q.e: The Earth's shadow causes eclipses, not phases.

q.t: More than half of the lit portion visible is called…
q.e: Crescent is less than half.

q.t: The waning period (bright part shrinking) is…
q.e: Waxing is Shukla Paksha.

q.t: A lunar eclipse can only happen on…
q.e: A solar eclipse needs a new Moon.

q.t: Why don't eclipses happen every month?
o: The Moon's orbit is slightly tilted
q.e: The Moon usually passes above or below the shadow line.

q.t: A waxing Moon is easiest to spot at…
q.e: A waning Moon at sunrise.

q.t: On full Moon day, the Moon is…
q.e: As the Sun rises, the full Moon sets.

q.t: A lunar year of 12 months is about how many days?
The extra month added in luni-solar calendars is…
q.e: The intercalary month.

q.t: The Indian National Calendar year begins on…
q.e: The day after the spring equinox (21 March in leap years).

q.t: A lunar year is about how many days shorter than the seasonal year (365 − 354)?
q.e: So seasons drift against lunar months.

q.t: Is 2024 a leap year?
Is 1900 a leap year?
o: No — century years must be divisible by 400
q.e: 1900 is skipped; 2000 was a leap year.

q.t: Why does the Moon rise ~50 minutes later each day?
o: It moves along its orbit, so Earth must turn a bit more
q.e: That's why the Moon is sometimes seen by day.

q.t: Why does everyone on Earth see nearly the same phase on a day?
o: Earth's rotation is much faster than the Moon's revolution
q.e: The Moon barely moves during one rotation.

q.t: The shadow of a vertical stick is shortest when…
q.e: Used to find the solar day.

q.t: Why do Diwali and Holi shift by less than a month each year?
o: Adhika Maasa keeps the luni-solar calendar near the seasons
q.e: The correction applies every few years.

q.t: Why does Eid-ul-Fitr drift about 11 days earlier each year?
o: It follows a purely lunar calendar with no correction
q.e: Over time it can fall in any month.

q.t: Makar Sankranti falls on nearly the same Gregorian date because it follows a…
q.e: Also Pongal, Bihu, Vaisakhi.

q.t: The sidereal year is longer than the tropical year by about…
q.e: So sidereal-calendar festivals slowly drift.

q.t: In the ball-and-lamp model, the ball held towards the lamp shows…
q.e: You see the dark side.

q.t: Uttarayan is the Sun's apparent movement…
q.e: Dakshinayan is southward.

q.t: In summer the Sun rises…
q.e: Extremes at the solstices.

q.t: Who chaired the 1952 Calendar Reform Committee?
q.e: Known for the Saha equation.

q.t: Most artificial satellites orbit about 800 km up, taking about how many minutes per orbit?
q.e: Much faster than the Moon.

q.t: Why are satellites seen just after sunset?
o: The sky is dark for you but the satellite still catches sunlight
q.e: Look for a steady moving point of light.

q.t: 'The Moon rises when the Sun sets' is true…
o: Only on a full Moon day
q.e: Otherwise moonrise is at a different time.

q.t: In Amant calendars, a month ends on…
q.e: Purnimant months end on the full Moon.

q.t: Space junk is a problem because…
o: It can collide with working satellites
q.e: Small pieces burn up; larger ones crowd space.

q.t: Why can a festival's date differ across India?
o: It depends on the lunar phase at local sunrise
q.e: Sunrise is earlier in the east.
